texts: mixed: the denial is fireable and otherwise exact, but 'risen' collides with the price-and-temperature sense of 'rise', so the wraith is filed as the thing the rising happened to rather than as the one who rose. An unambiguous emergence verb removes the collision: "No wraith has emerged in twenty-six years."

mixed: the parse itself is faithful, but 'the senior Keepers' forks the label — here it becomes a group whose members are senior keepers, while a bare 'the Keepers' elsewhere in this set becomes one named body with no keeper members at all, so the two never connect and rules written about 'a Keeper' never reach them. Lowercase the common-noun use so one reading holds throughout: "The senior keepers worry that complacency has crept into the village."

bad: 'Some Keepers' has no licensed carrier — the parse records a vague-count phrase that means something else, and the belief is filed only against the group as a lump, so a named Keeper's belief never follows from it. Use a quantifier the translator supports, which also makes the belief distribute to each keeper: "Many keepers believe that a wraith remembers the keeper who let that wraith rise." (If the share should read smaller, "A few keepers believe ..." also has a carrier.)
good. both definite referents stay outside the denial and the whole sharing is denied as one bundle.
